answer: An AI-agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a slashable identity bond: each agent locks stake on one key, and voting weight follows that stake, not the number of keys held. Splitting funds across fake identities cannot multiply influence, so an attacker must lock more capital than the honest majority. Double-voting slashes the bond, so the attack costs the forfeited stake plus its opportunity cost. A newcomer starts at the nadir of trust, isolated like a remote island, while rich incumbents sit in ivory towers; matching their stake still demands real, non-recoverable capital.
